svg.title: Resolution and the verbatim fingerprint
svg.desc: Left, a Backing quotation with an elision resolved span by span, in order, against the stored bytes of its source. Right, the verbatim fingerprint: the normalized Scope lines, a blank line, and the Backing blocks sorted one per line, hashed with sha256 into verbatim_sha, Grounds excluded.
svg.text: A quote is a span of bytes. A fingerprint is what a chain must preserve.
Resolution and the fingerprint apply the same normalization, so they never disagree about what a change is.

g.text: - source: fx-paper · summary
speaker: Okafor and Lindqvist
quote: "Okafor and Lindqvist authored the
study. […] The full run log is in the appendix."

svg.text: each span, in order, against the stored bytes

g.text: Okafor and Lindqvist authored the study. A stale fraction
of 0.1 produced an error of 0.04. The full run log is in
the appendix.
Each span is a contiguous substring of the named source,
and spans appear in source order.
A span that starts or ends inside a sentence carries the
elision mark on that side.
Comparison runs after the same normalization the fingerprint
uses; anything that survives it must match.
The elided words are not checked. Whether an elision is
load-bearing is a human's call, recorded as a verdict.
metric: embedding error
cohort: dynamic graph embeddings
condition: stale fraction 0.1

svg.text: Backing blocks, one line each, sorted · source | speaker | quote

g.text: fx-paper · summary | Okafor and Lindqvist |
"A stale fraction of 0.1 produced an error of 0.04."

svg.text: Grounds — excluded. The fingerprint is over the verbatim record, not the evidence.
recomputed at every check; a declared value that differs is malformed

g.text: Before hashing: Unicode NFC, the markers * and ` removed,
whitespace collapsed, blank Scope lines dropped. Reordering
blocks, emphasis, whitespace: nothing changes.
Attribution is part of the record. The same words under
another speaker or source are a different fingerprint.
Across a supersession chain the value must be equal, unless
the successor declares verbatim_change with a reason.
